resources.string: Add a WireGuard config to route individual connection profiles through it — no system-wide VPN required.
Remove \"%1$s\". Profiles referencing this tunnel will fail to connect until you pick another one.

Paste a wg-quick style config or load a .conf file. Only [Interface] and [Peer] fields are read; unknown keys (PostUp, Table, MTU) are ignored. Hostname endpoints and DNS names are resolved at tunnel start.

Generate an authkey in the Tailscale admin console (Settings → Keys), or in your Headscale CLI (`headscale preauthkeys create`). Haven joins your tailnet on first use and reuses the node state after that, so a one-time key is fine. Reusable keys let you reconnect after reinstall.
Leave blank for Tailscale\'s hosted controlplane. Set to a Headscale URL for a self-hosted coordination server.

Generate a setup key in the NetBird dashboard (Setup Keys → Add setup key). Haven joins your network on first use and reuses the peer state after that, so a one-time key is fine. Reusable keys let you reconnect after reinstall.
Leave blank for NetBird\'s hosted management. Set to your server\'s URL for a self-hosted management service.
Paste an .ovpn profile or load a file. If the profile uses auth-user-pass without an inline credentials file, enter a username and password below.
Experimental — Haven implements the same WebSocket wire protocol as `cloudflared access ssh`. Tested against a small set of tenants; please report mismatches via GitHub #154.

Route SSH through a Cloudflare Tunnel published hostname — the in-app equivalent of `cloudflared access ssh --hostname <host>`. Public Tunnel routes need only a hostname. Access-protected routes additionally require a JWT — tap Sign in to capture one via your team\'s IdP.
No JWT — only works for unprotected Tunnel routes
Only needed for Access-protected routes; lets us capture the team-domain cookie as a fallback if the per-app one is missing.
Bastion-mode multi-target tunnels: forwarded as `Cf-Access-Jump-Destination`. Leave blank for one-target routes.
For headless setups: run `cloudflared access token --app https://<hostname>` on another machine and paste the JWT here. Expiry is parsed from the token automatically.

Connect through a Cisco AnyConnect or ocserv (OpenConnect) VPN without the Cisco app. Only profiles that route through this tunnel use it; the rest of your phone does not. Username/password, auth groups and TOTP or push second factors are supported; SAML/SSO and client certificates are not.
Gateway host as you would type it into Cisco\'s app, optionally with :port or a group path.
The group or profile to choose from the server\'s list. Leave blank for the default.
Base32 secret or otpauth:// link from your authenticator setup. Haven answers the code prompt itself, which lets the tunnel reconnect unattended.
A fixed answer to the second prompt, e.g. push for Duo. Used only when no OTP secret is set.
Only for self-signed gateways: a pin-sha256:… value. If the certificate is not trusted, the connection error shows the value to paste here.
Leave empty to be asked when signing in.
Codes sent by SMS or e-mail: leave the OTP secret and second-factor answer empty, and Haven asks for the code when you sign in.
Keep the VPN up after your last connection closes, like Cisco\'s app. Off: it disconnects, and reconnecting soon after resumes the session without a new code.
